raw.info: FIN7 is deploying memory-scraping point-of-sale malware against US department-store chains, harvesting track data from card transactions on Windows 11 POS terminals during the holiday shopping season.

A Magecart web skimmer campaign is injecting formjacking scripts into the Nginx-fronted checkout pages of North American e-commerce retailers, exfiltrating cardholder data from online apparel and homewares stores.
ESXiArgs-style ransomware is encrypting VMware ESXi 8.0 and vSphere datastores at mid-market merchants in the United States, disabling snapshots and crippling both store and e-commerce workloads.

Scattered Spider operators are running spear-phishing and help-desk social engineering against Microsoft Entra ID tenants of US and Canadian retailers to achieve account takeover and lateral movement into Azure.

Credential-stuffing operators are targeting retail loyalty programme portals backed by PostgreSQL, using leaked credential datasets to commit gift-card and loyalty fraud against omnichannel apparel merchants.

Operators at a municipal water-treatment facility in rural Bavaria detected unauthorised changes to chemical-dosing PLC logic, forcing a manual shutdown of the filtration line while engineers restored safe setpoints.

Several cargo vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz reported GPS positions drifting miles off course, consistent with a coordinated spoofing campaign targeting maritime satellite navigation systems.
A flaw in solar-powered irrigation controllers used across Kenyan smallholder farms allowed attackers to remotely open and close water valves, disrupting planting schedules for the coming season.

A safety-controller flaw in welding robots on a Japanese automotive assembly line allowed cycle-timing manipulation that could damage chassis components mid-weld, prompting an emergency production halt.
After years of drought breaks across the outback, record rains caused two ageing dams to overflow and several pipelines to spring leaks, displacing hundreds of residents over the long weekend.
Geologists surveying the Atacama announced fresh lithium deposits uncovered after decades of mineral exposure gradually reshaped the dry basin floor.
Dockers at the Port of Rotterdam walked off the job for three days, leaving dozens of container ships idling offshore amid a long-running pay dispute.
A countryside falconry festival drew record crowds this spring as handlers demonstrated peregrine and goshawk hunting displays across the moors.
Thousands gathered at the central entrance of the new national library for its gala opening, with the mayor cutting the ribbon before a public reading.
A regional clothing chain discovered that the checkout tills in dozens of its shops had been quietly infected with software that copied shoppers' credit and debit details at the moment of payment.

Investigators found that someone had slipped hidden code into the online checkout pages of a homewares seller, so each completed order silently forwarded the buyer's payment details to an outside server.

Attackers broke into the virtualisation cluster that runs a high-street chain's tills and warehouse systems, scrambled the virtual machines, wiped the backups, and demanded a payment to restore access.
A surge of automated sign-in attempts using stolen username and password lists hammered a shopping rewards website over the weekend, locking tens of thousands of members out of their points balances.

Employees at a fashion store group were hit with realistic emails that tricked several into entering their work logins on a fake page, handing attackers access to the company's cloud mailboxes and staff directory.
Ransomware operators are actively exploiting a VMware ESXi vulnerability to break out of guest virtual machines and encrypt hypervisor datastores; the flaw is now in CISA's KEV catalog.
An authentication-bypass vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS is being weaponised in the wild to gain super-admin access to FortiGate firewalls and stage further intrusion.
Attackers are chaining a Windows SmartScreen bypass to drop payment-card scraping malware onto retail point-of-sale terminals running Windows 11; the bug is under active exploitation.
A PostgreSQL flaw permitting environment-variable manipulation and code execution is being probed against internet-exposed database backends holding customer records.
The Outlook privilege-escalation bug continues to be exploited via crafted calendar invites to steal NTLM credentials from Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online users with no click required.
A critical Cisco IOS XE web UI vulnerability is under mass exploitation to implant backdoors on enterprise edge routers across multiple sectors worldwide.
